entities.name: Amantius of Como
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Amantius of Como was the third bishop of Como, succeeding Felix and being succeeded by Abundius. He played a role in the governance of the Diocese of Como during the 5th century AD.

Born around 400 AD, Amantius served as bishop from approximately 440 to 448 AD. During his tenure, he contributed to the religious and cultural life of the diocese.

Amantius's legacy includes the preservation of Christian traditions in the region, which continued to thrive after his death. His feast day is celebrated on April 8th.

The significance of Amantius lies in his role as a stabilizing figure during a period of political instability and religious persecution in Western Europe.
